claim: Under stress conditions, EAE caused severe gastrointestinal failure with high-mortality.
source: Under stress conditions, EAE caused severe gastrointestinal failure with high-mortality.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing clinical scores, mortality rates, and gastrointestinal pathology in EAE mice under stress conditions.

claim: Autoreactive-pathogenic CD4+ T cells accumulated at specific vessels of boundary area of third-ventricle, thalamus, and dentate-gyrus to establish brain micro-inflammation via stress-gateway reflex.
source: Mechanistically, autoreactive-pathogenic CD4+ T cells accumulated at specific vessels of boundary area of third-ventricle, thalamus, and dentate-gyrus to establish brain micro-inflammation via stress-gateway reflex.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data and flow cytometry showing CD4+ T cell accumulation at specific brain vessels under stress conditions.

claim: Induction of brain micro-inflammation at specific vessels by cytokine injection was sufficient to establish fatal gastrointestinal failure.
source: Importantly, induction of brain micro-inflammation at specific vessels by cytokine injection was sufficient to establish fatal gastrointestinal failure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that direct microinjection of cytokines at specific brain vessels induced gastrointestinal failure and mortality.

claim: Resulting micro-inflammation activated new neural pathway including neurons in paraventricular-nucleus, dorsomedial-nucleus-of-hypothalamus, and also vagal neurons to cause fatal gastrointestinal failure.
source: Resulting micro-inflammation activated new neural pathway including neurons in paraventricular-nucleus, dorsomedial-nucleus-of-hypothalamus, and also vagal neurons to cause fatal gastrointestinal failure.
evidence: This claim is supported by neural tracing experiments and immunohistochemical data showing activation of PVN, DMH, and vagal neurons following brain micro-inflammation.

claim: Suppression of the brain micro-inflammation or blockage of these neural pathways inhibited the gastrointestinal failure.
source: Suppression of the brain micro-inflammation or blockage of these neural pathways inhibited the gastrointestinal failure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that interventions blocking inflammation or neural pathways reduced gastrointestinal pathology and mortality.

claim: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoreactive helper T cell (CD4+ T cell)-mediated autoimmune disease in the central nervous system (CNS) (Sawcer et al., 2011).
source: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoreactive helper T cell (CD4+ T cell)-mediated autoimmune disease in the central nervous system (CNS) (Sawcer et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature on MS pathogenesis.

claim: MS can be divided into at least four subgroups: relapse-remitting MS (over 80% patients), secondary progressive MS, primary progressive MS (about 10% patients), and relapse-progressing MS (about 5% patients).
source: It can be divided into at least four subgroups: (1) relapse-remitting MS (over 80% patients), (2) secondary progressive MS (the late phase of relapse-remitting type), (3) primary progressive MS (about 10% patients), and (4) relapse-progressing MS (about 5% patients), all of which are characterized by chronic inflammation in the CNS (Steinman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature on MS classification.

claim: MS inflammatory lesions consist of various immune cells, including CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+CD11b+ monocytes/macrophages.
source: MS inflammatory lesions consist of various immune cells, including CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+CD11b+ monocytes/macrophages, and subsequent loss of neurological function in the CNS due to the disruption of neural circuits that regulate various organ functions (Steinman, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established literature on MS pathology.

claim: Several complications including mental illnesses and gastrointestinal failures are associated with MS.
source: Indeed, several complications including mental illnesses and gastrointestinal failures are associated with MS (Goldman Consensus Group, 2005; Gupta et al., 2005; Kimura et al., 2000; Marrie et al., 2015; Pokorny et al., 2007; Rang et al., 1982; Sadovnick et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to literature documenting MS complications.

claim: EAE development is dependent on autoreactive helper T cells (pathogenic CD4+ T cells), particularly Th1 and Th17 cells.
source: EAE development is dependent on autoreactive helper T cells (pathogenic CD4+ T cells), particularly Th1 and Th17 cells and many immune cells are accumulated at the affected sites such as CD8+ T cells, macrophages, B cells, and neutrophils. (Arima et al., 2012, 2015; Jäger et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on EAE pathogenesis.

claim: The transfer EAE model is completely dependent on MOG-specific CD4+ T cells (pathogenic CD4+ T cells) including Th17 and Th1 populations, while it is not dependent on CD8+ T cells.
source: Therefore, the transfer EAE model is completely dependent on MOG-specific CD4+ T cells (pathogenic CD4+ T cells) including Th17 and Th1 populations, while it is not dependent on CD8+ T cells because of no CD8+ T cells in the transferred pathogenic T cell population.
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental design where only CD4+ T cells are transferred, logically excluding CD8+ T cell dependence.

claim: There are many papers that describe the involvement of not only IL-17A but also IFN-γ particularly from pathogenic CD4+ T cells including activated Th1 and Th17 cells for the development of EAE models.
source: Importantly, there are many papers that describe the involvement of not only IL-17A but also IFN-γ particularly from pathogenic CD4+ T cells including activated Th1 and Th17 cells for the development of EAE models including the transfer EAE ones (Duhen et al., 2013; El-behi et al., 2010; Goverman, 2009; Jäger et al., 2009; Ottum et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to literature on cytokine involvement in EAE.

claim: Stress conditions can cause gastrointestinal diseases via the brain-gut axis.
source: Stress conditions can cause gastrointestinal diseases via the brain-gut axis.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field of brain-gut interactions.

claim: The brain-gut axis involves interactions between neural components, including the autonomic nervous system, the central nervous system, the stress system such as the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and the corticotropin-releasing factor system, and intestinal factors.
source: Animal models have shown that this axis involves interactions between neural components, including the autonomic nervous system, the central nervous system, the stress system such as the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and the corticotropin-releasing factor system, and intestinal factors such as the intestinal barrier, the luminal microbiota, and the intestinal immune response (Allen et al., 2014; Bonaz and Bernstein, 2013; Caso et al., 2008; Stengel and Taché, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on brain-gut axis mechanisms.

claim: Details about the underlying molecular mechanisms, including the relationship between each of these components, are lacking.
source: However, details about the underlying molecular mechanisms, including the relationship between each of these components, are lacking.
evidence: This claim represents a knowledge gap identified by the authors based on literature review.

claim: Brain micro-inflammation at blood vessels specific in the boundary area of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus is established by pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress conditions.
source: We demonstrate that brain micro-inflammation at blood vessels specific in the boundary area of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus is established by pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress conditions and induces fatal gastrointestinal failure via a paraventricular nucleus (PVN)/dorsomedial nucleus of the hypothalamus (DMH)-vagal pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing immune cell accumulation at specific brain vessels under stress conditions.

claim: The gateway reflex triggered by stress-mediated PVN activation induced the accumulation of immune cells at specific vessels in a manner dependent on CCL5.
source: Mechanistic analysis suggested that the gateway reflex triggered by stress-mediated PVN activation induced the accumulation of immune cells, including pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells, at these specific vessels in a manner dependent on CCL5.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing CCL5 expression at specific vessels and the effect of CCL5 blockade on immune cell accumulation.

claim: The resulting brain micro-inflammation enhanced a new neural pathway including neurons in the PVN and DMH, and vagal nerve-mediated gastrointestinal failure via micro-inflammation-dependent ATP.
source: The resulting brain micro-inflammation enhanced a new neural pathway including neurons in the PVN and DMH, and vagal nerve-mediated gastrointestinal failure via micro-inflammation-dependent ATP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing ATP production, neural activation, and the effects of ATP receptor blockade.

claim: Blockade of the regional brain micro-inflammation and establishment of the new neural pathway inhibited the gastrointestinal pathology.
source: Accordingly, blockade of the regional brain micro-inflammation and establishment of the new neural pathway inhibited the gastrointestinal pathology.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing therapeutic effects of various interventions.

claim: Pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under the stress condition caused a severe phenotype including sudden death.
source: Pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under the stress condition of the current study caused a severe phenotype including sudden death (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by clinical score and mortality data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Either stress or pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer alone did not cause the severe phenotype.
source: On the other hand, either stress or pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer alone, or stress with the transfer of activated CD4+ T cells specific for irrelevant antigens such as ovalbumin or a retinal autoantigen, interphotoreceptor retinoid-binding protein (IRBP), did not cause the severe phenotype, although the retina-specific activated CD4+ T cells accumulated in the eyes (Figure 1A and B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing different treatment groups shown in figures.

claim: Blood aldosterone and cortisol levels were significantly higher in mice with stress even without pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer.
source: Blood aldosterone and cortisol levels were significantly higher in mice with stress even without pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B), suggesting stress-mediated activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis.
evidence: This claim is supported by hormone measurement data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Chronic stress conditions cause a severe and atypical phenotype of EAE, which might represent progressive MS.
source: These results demonstrate that chronic stress conditions cause a severe and atypical phenotype of EAE, which might represent progressive MS.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from experimental data and comparison to MS clinical presentations.

claim: Mice induced with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress excreted bloody stools.
source: We noticed that mice induced with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress, but not either treatment only, excreted bloody stools (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fecal occult blood test data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Blood hematocrit levels decreased in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress.
source: Consistently, blood hematocrit levels decreased (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by hematocrit measurement data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The blood content came from the stomach and upper level of the intestine.
source: We found the blood content came from the stomach and upper level of the intestine (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by tissue analysis data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Focal bleeding lesions in the stomach were detected by histopathological analysis.
source: Focal bleeding lesions in the stomach were detected by histopathological analysis (Figure 2D, black spots), and tissue distraction including epithelial necrosis was evident particularly in the stomach and upper level of the intestine (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by histopathological data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: Under very strong stress, the activation of p38 and MAPKAPK2 contributes to stomach epithelial destruction under muscarinic M3 receptor signaling via acetyocholine derived from vagus nerve.
source: It has been reported that under very strong stress, the activation of p38 and MAPKAPK2 contributes to stomach epithelial destruction under muscarinic M3 receptor signaling via acetyocholine derived from vagus nerve (Debas and Carvajal, 1994; Jia et al., 2007; Uwada et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on stress-induced gastric pathology.

claim: Phosphorylated p38 and phosphorylated MAPKAPK2 were detected in the gastric mucosa of mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: We investigated the activation status of p38 and MAPKAPK2 in stomach isolated from mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under our stress condition and detected phosphorylated p38 and phosphorylated MAPKAPK2 in the gastric mucosa (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treatment with a proton pump inhibitor, lansoprazol, suppressed the severe phenotype in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: Consistent with dysregulation of gastrointestinal region, the treatment with a proton pump inhibitor, lansoprazol, suppressed the severe phenotype in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing therapeutic effects of lansoprazol shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Increase of plasma potassium levels was observed in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: Furthermore, increase of plasma potassium levels, most likely following the gastrointestinal bleeding, was observed in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by plasma potassium measurement data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Heart failure was detected in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition by a cardiac electrocardiogram system.
source: Heart failure was detected in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition by a cardiac electrocardiogram system (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting a heart failure at least partially mediated by high potassium ions.
evidence: This claim is supported by ECG data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Donor pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells first accumulate at the L5 cord within 5 days after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer via the gravity-gateway reflex.
source: Donor pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells first accumulate at the L5 cord within 5 days after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer via the gravity-gateway reflex as described previously (Arima et al., 2012; Sabharwal et al., 2014) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3A and citations to previous work.

claim: Chronic stress caused pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells to accumulate at specific vessels of the boundary region of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus, but not in the L5 cord.
source: In the present work, chronic stress caused pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells to accumulate at specific vessels of the boundary region of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus, but not in the L5 cord (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The L5 cord vessels are no longer used as a gateway for immune cells toward the CNS under chronic stress conditions.
source: These data suggested that the L5 cord vessels are no longer used as a gateway for immune cells toward the CNS under chronic stress conditions.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that immune cells do not accumulate at L5 under stress conditions.

claim: Pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells accumulated comparably at the brain specific vessels regardless of lansoprazol treatment in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: We also found that pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class II+ cells accumulated comparably at the brain specific vessels redardless of lansoprazol treatment, which suppressed gastrointestine dysregulation (see Fiugre 2F), in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells originated from the peripheral organs rather than resident microglia cells.
source: Td-tomato labeling of microglia cells, which we used previously (Arima et al., 2015), revealed that MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells originated from the peripheral organs rather than resident microglia cells (Figure 3D), suggesting that the MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells that accumulated at the specific vessels were activated monocytes from the peripheral organs.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell lineage tracing data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Various immune cells, including CD8+ T cells, B cells, NK cells, and neutrophils, had accumulated at the specific vessels.
source: Moreover, we found that various immune cells, including CD8+ T cells, B cells, NK cells, and neutrophils, had also accumulated at the specific vessels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Blockade of CCL5 significantly suppressed the accumulation of pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells at the specific vessels.
source: Blockade of CCL5, but not chemokines including CCL2, CX3CL1, significantly suppressed the accumulation of pathogenic CD4+ T cells and MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells at the specific vessels (Figure 4A and B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and reduced clinical scores and mortality (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of CCL5 neutralization shown in Figures 4A, B, and C.

claim: The stress condition even without pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer induced CCL5 expression at the specific blood vessels.
source: Interestingly, the stress condition even without pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer induced CCL5 expression at the specific blood vessels, but acute stress models did not. (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data showing CCL5 mRNA expression shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Neutralization of IFN-γ or IL-17A inhibited the brain micro-inflammation at the specific vessels.
source: Moreover, neutralization of the Th1 cytokine, interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), or that of the Th17 cytokine, IL-17A, also inhibited the brain micro-inflammation at the specific vessels (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of cytokine neutralization shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The accumulation of IL-17A- or IFN-γ-deficient pathogenic CD4+ T cells was significantly reduced at the specific blood vessels under stress conditions.
source: Importantly, the accumulation of IL-17A- or IFN-γ-deficient pathogenic CD4+ T cells was significantly reduced at the specific blood vessels under stress conditions and resulted in less mortality (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using cytokine-deficient T cells shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Both IFN-γ and IL-17A from pathogenic CD4+ T cells are necessary for the accumulation at specific vessels and the severe phenotypes.
source: These data suggested that both IFN-γ and IL-17A from pathogenic CD4+ T cells are necessary for the accumulation at specific vessels and the severe phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data showing effects of cytokine deficiency and neutralization.

claim: Brain micro-inflammation induced by microinjection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells plus MOG-pulsed DC or inflammatory cytokines at specific vessels developed severe gastrointestinal failure and affected mortality.
source: We found that brain micro-inflammation induced by these treatments developed severe gastrointestinal failure and affected mortality (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of direct cytokine injection shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Anti-CCL5 antibody treatment had no significant effect on mortality of mice with microinjections of cytokines at the specific vessels under stress condition.
source: Furthermore, we investigated the mortality of mice with microinjections of cytokines at the specific vessels under stress condition in the presence or absence of anti-CCL5 antibody treatment and found anti-CCL5 antibody treatment had no significant effect (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: CCL5 mainly contributes to the accumulation of immune cells including pathogenic CD4+ T cells at the specific vessels, while the effect of cytokine injection is CCL5-independent.
source: This result suggested that CCL5 mainly contributes to the accumulation of immune cells including pathogenic CD4+ T cells at the specific vessels, while the effect of cytokine injection is CCL5-independent.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that CCL5 blockade does not affect cytokine-induced pathology.

claim: Microinjection of 6-OHDA at the specific vessels successfully depleted TH+ sympathetic neurons and phospho-CREB signals.
source: Microinjection of 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) at the specific vessels successfully depleted tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)+ sympathetic neurons and phospho-CREB signals that were induced by noradrenergic receptor signaling after sympathetic activation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: 6-OHDA-mediated chemical sympathectomy suppressed immune cell accumulation at the specific vessels and the development of fatal gastrointestinal failure.
source: 6-OHDA-mediated chemical sympathectomy suppressed immune cell accumulation at the specific vessels and the development of fatal gastrointestinal failure in mice that received pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 5A–5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of sympathectomy shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: PVN neurons include TH+ neurons that are activated by several stresses, especially chronic ones.
source: It is reported that PVN neurons include TH+ neurons are activated by several stresses, especially chronic ones (Herman and Cullinan, 1997; Ramot et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2013; Ulrich-Lai and Herman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on PVN neuron activation.

claim: PVN TH+ neurons were specifically activated by stress condition even without EAE induction.
source: Consistent with these results, we found that PVN TH+ neurons were specifically activated by stress condition even without EAE induction (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The activation of PVN neurons, particularly THneg neurons, was enhanced in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: Moreover, the activation of PVN neurons, particularly THneg neurons, was enhanced in mice with pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 5C), suggesting the crosstalk between microinflammation at the specifc vessels and PVN.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Injection of a retrograde neural tracer, cholera toxin B (CTB), at specific vessels reached the PVN.
source: We found that injection of a retrograde neural tracer, cholera toxin B (CTB), at specific vessels of the boundary area of third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus reached the PVN (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by neural tracing data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: TH+ neurons at the PVN co-expressed noradrenaline transporter, but not dopamine transporter.
source: In addition, TH+ neurons at the PVN co-expressed noradrenaline transporter, but not dopamine transporter (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that they secrete noradrenaline at the specific vessels, which we have shown to be important for chemokine induction (Arima et al., 2012, 2015; Sabharwal et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: An anterograde tracer, PHA-L, injected at specific vessels mainly reached the DMH and to a lesser degree the PVN.
source: We found that an anterograde tracer, PHA-L, injected at these vessels mainly reached the DMH and to a lesser degree the PVN (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by neural tracing data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CTB injection at the DMH region reached the specific vessels.
source: Consistent with this result, CTB injection at the DMH region reached the specific vessels (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by neural tracing data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: DMH neurons, particularly THneg ones, were highly activated after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition.
source: Importantly, DMH neurons, particularly THneg ones, were highly activated after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer under stress condition (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The injection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells plus MOG-pulsed DC or IL-17A plus IFN-γ cytokines at the specific vessels under stress condition enhanced neural activation of the PVN and DMH.
source: Consistent with this notion, the injection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells plus MOG-pulsed DC or IL-17A plus IFN-γ cytokines at the specific vessels under stress condition enhanced neural activation of the PVN and DMH (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The ablation of PVN and DMH sites significantly inhibited brain micro-inflammation, gastrointestinal disease and mortality.
source: Furthermore, the ablation of PVN and DMH sites significantly inhibited brain micro-inflammation, gastrointestinal disease and mortality (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of neural ablation shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The activation of DMH neurons is suppressed by GABA-A receptor activation.
source: It is reported that the activation of DMH neurons is suppressed by GABA-A receptor activation (Rusyniak et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on DMH neuron regulation.

claim: Muscimol injection at DMH suppressed gastrointestinal disease and mortality.
source: Muscimol, GABA-A receptor agonist, injection at DMH suppressed gastrointestinal disease and mortality (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of muscimol treatment shown in Figure 5I.

claim: DMH activation following the microinflammation at the specific vessels is critical for the development of fatal gastrointestinal disease.
source: All these results suggested that DMH activation following the microinflammation at the specific vessels is critical for the development of fatal gastrointestinal disease.
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple experimental results showing the role of DMH in pathology.

claim: ATP is a neurotransmitter and is expressed in several cells after cytokine stimulation.
source: ATP is a neurotransmitter and is expressed in several cells after cytokine stimulation (Burnstock, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on ATP function.

claim: The expression of ATP was enhanced after IL-17A plus IL-6 stimulation in endothelial cells in vitro.
source: We found that the expression of ATP was enhanced after IL-17A plus IL-6 stimulation in endothelial cells in vitro (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Neurons in the DMH were highly activated by the microinjection of ATP at the specific vessels under stress condition.
source: Neurons in the DMH were highly activated by the microinjection of ATP at the specific vessels under stress condition (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Blockade of the ATP receptor, P2RX7, at the specific vessels by A438079 suppressed the neural activation and fatal gastrointestinal failure.
source: Moreover, blockade of the ATP receptor, P2RX7, at the specific vessels by A438079, a selective antagonist, suppressed the neural activation and fatal gastrointestinal failure (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of P2RX7 blockade shown in Figures 6B and C.

claim: Neurons around the specific vessels expressed P2RX7.
source: Neurons (Neurofilament L-positive cells) around the specific vessels expressed P2RX7 and after cytokine or ATP stimulation, neurons in the DMH region also showed NFATc1 activation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), which is a downstream signaling component of P2RX7 (Grol et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: NFATc1 is a downstream signaling component of P2RX7.
source: Neurons (Neurofilament L-positive cells) around the specific vessels expressed P2RX7 and after cytokine or ATP stimulation, neurons in the DMH region also showed NFATc1 activation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), which is a downstream signaling component of P2RX7 (Grol et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on P2RX7 signaling.

claim: ATP can be sensed by neurons that connect specific vessels to the DMH region in a manner dependent on P2RX7 expression.
source: Thus, we suggested that ATP can be sensed by neurons that connect specific vessels to the DMH region in a manner dependent on P2RX7 expression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data showing P2RX7 expression and ATP effects.

claim: The status of PVN neurons affects the homeostasis of gastrointestinal organs via branches of the vagal nerves.
source: We next investigated whether vagal nerve activation is involved in the development of the severe gastrointestinal failure triggered by brain micro-inflammation, because (i) the status of PVN neurons affects the homeostasis of gastrointestinal organs via branches of the vagal nerves (Ferguson et al., 1988) and (ii) the DMH is connected to the vagal neurons at the dorsal motor vagal nucleus (DMX), where the nucleus of the vagal nerves are present (Thompson et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on PVN-vagal connections.

claim: The DMH is connected to the vagal neurons at the dorsal motor vagal nucleus (DMX).
source: We next investigated whether vagal nerve activation is involved in the development of the severe gastrointestinal failure triggered by brain micro-inflammation, because (i) the status of PVN neurons affects the homeostasis of gastrointestinal organs via branches of the vagal nerves (Ferguson et al., 1988) and (ii) the DMH is connected to the vagal neurons at the dorsal motor vagal nucleus (DMX), where the nucleus of the vagal nerves are present (Thompson et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on DMH-DMX connections.

claim: PHA-L after injection at the DMH reached the DMX.
source: PHA-L after injection at the DMH reached the DMX as described (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by neural tracing data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The DMX is highly activated after the injection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells with MOG-pulsed DC at the vessels under stress condition.
source: Moreover, we found that the DMX is highly activated after the injection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells with MOG-pulsed DC at the vessels of the boundary area of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus under stress condition (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Nucleus of the Tractus Solitaries (NTS) was activated after injection of pathogenic CD4+ T cells with MOG-pulsed DC at the vessels under stress condition.
source: In addition, we found that Nucleus of the Tractus Solitaries (NTS), which is the main nucleus of afferent vagus nerves, was activated (Figure 7A), suggesting that afferent neuronal activation is induced by severe gastrointestinal failure, most likely in a manner dependent on micro-inflammation-related ATP in gastrointestinal regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Vagotomy suppressed gastrointestinal failure and mortality in EAE mice under stress.
source: Finally, we found that vagotomy suppressed gastrointestinal failure and mortality in EAE mice under stress (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of vagotomy shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Severe gastrointestinal failure is induced by enhanced neural activation via the DMH-vagal axis, which is activated by brain micro-inflammation at the specific vessels under stress.
source: These results suggest that severe gastrointestinal failure is induced by enhanced neural activation via the DMH-vagal axis, which is activated by brain micro-inflammation at the specific vessels under stress.
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple experimental results showing the neural pathway involved in pathology.

claim: Brain micro-inflammation at the boundary area of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus develops severe gastrointestinal failure via the DMH-vagal pathway in a transfer EAE model under stress.
source: We here showed that brain micro-inflammation at the boundary area of the third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus develops severe gastrointestinal failure via the DMH-vagal pathway in a transfer EAE model under stress.
evidence: This claim summarizes the main findings supported by multiple experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pathogenic CD4+ T cells transverse toward the central nervous system (CNS) through a gateway at the dorsal vessels of the fifth lumbar (L5) spinal cord in steady state in response to gravity-mediated chemokine expression via regional sympathetic activation, a phenomenon called the gravity-gateway reflex.
source: We have reported that pathogenic CD4+ T cells transverse toward the central nervous system (CNS) through a gateway at the dorsal vessels of the fifth lumbar (L5) spinal cord in steady state in response to gravity-mediated chemokine expression via regional sympathetic activation, a phenomenon we call the gravity-gateway reflex (Arima et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Artificial electric stimulations in different muscles establishes the immune cell gateways at different regions of the dorsal vessels of spinal cord, a phenomenon called the electric-gateway reflex.
source: During the gravity-gateway reflex, we found that artificial electric stimulations in different muscles, which mimic specific sensory-sympathetic crosstalk, establsihes the immune cell gateways at different regions of the dorsal vessels of spinal cord, a phenomenon we call the electric-gateway reflex (Arima et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Pain induces sympathetic-mediated alterations in ventral vessels of the spinal cord to establish gateways to cause EAE relapse, a phenomenon called the pain-gateway reflex.
source: We also found that pain induces sympathetic-mediated alterations in ventral vessels of the spinal cord to establish gateways to cause EAE relapse, a phenomenon we call the pain-gateway reflex (Arima et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Under stress condition, a gateway forms at the vessels of boundary area of third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus, which is described as the stress-gateway reflex.
source: In the present study, we show that, under stress condition, a gateway forms at the vessels of boundary area of third ventricle region, thalamus, and dentate gyrus, which we describe as the stress-gateway reflex.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing immune cell accumulation at specific brain vessels under stress.

claim: Mice with stress show reduced movement and often lie down.
source: Because we found that mice with stress show reduced movement and often lie down, we hypothesize they would have reduced stimulation of the soleus muscles, which are the main anti-gravity muscles.
evidence: This claim is based on observation of mouse behavior under stress conditions.

claim: Mice with stress reduce L5 DRG activation and chemokine expression from L5 dorsal vessels.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, we found that mice with stress reduce L5 DRG activation and chemokine expression from L5 dorsal vessels (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Stress condition reduces anti-gravity-mediated soleus stimulation followed by closing the L5 gateway of immune cells.
source: Thus, it is possible that stress condition reduces anti-gravity-mediated soleus stimulation followed by closing the L5 gateway of immune cells.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from behavioral observations and molecular data.

claim: CX3CL1 is a key chemokine for the accumulation of activated monocytes at L5 ventral vessels and EAE relapse after pain induction in EAE-recovered mice.
source: In our previous work, we identified CX3CL1 as a key chemokine for the accumulation of activated monocytes at L5 ventral vessels and EAE relapse after pain induction in EAE-recovered mice (Arima et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Over 90% of MS patients experience relapse.
source: On the other hand, over 90% of MS patients experience relapse, and there are reports showing that the occurrence of pain is associated with neurologic symptoms and disease severity in patients with MS (Ehde et al., 2003, 2006; O'Connor et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature on MS.

claim: The occurrence of pain is associated with neurologic symptoms and disease severity in patients with MS.
source: On the other hand, over 90% of MS patients experience relapse, and there are reports showing that the occurrence of pain is associated with neurologic symptoms and disease severity in patients with MS (Ehde et al., 2003, 2006; O'Connor et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature on MS.

claim: Many MHC class IIhiCX3CR1+CD11b+ cells are found in the CNS particularly in L5 level of EAE-recovered mice.
source: In the EAE-recovered mice, many MHC class IIhiCX3CR1+CD11b+ cells are found in the CNS particulalry in L5 level.
evidence: This claim is based on previous experimental observations by the authors.

claim: MHC class IIhiCX3CR1+CD11b+ cells in EAE-recovered mice are not activated microglial cells but activated monocytes coming from the periphery.
source: These cells are not activated microglial cells but activated monocytes coming from the periphery.
evidence: This claim is based on lineage tracing experiments described in previous work.

claim: Activated monocytes in the CNS of EAE-recovered mice stayed for a long time (over 150 days in some cases) after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer.
source: Importantly, these activated monocytes in the CNS of EAE-recovered mice stayed for a long time (over 150 days in some cases) after pathogenic CD4+ T cell transfer and are critical for the development of pain-mediated EAE relapse (Arima et al., 2015), eLife).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Resident T cells stay in non-immune tissues for a very long time (over 150 days in some cases) after the initial immune response in the tissues and affect subsequent immune responses.
source: On the other hand, many papers have recently reported resident T cells stay in non-immune tissues for a very long time (over 150 days in some cases) after the initial immune response in the tissues and affect subsequent immune responses (Iijima and Iwasaki, 2014; Mueller and Mackay, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on tissue-resident immune cells.

claim: The origin of the resident monocytes could be patrolling monocytes with CX3CR1 in blood stream.
source: Therefore, it is possible that the origin of the resident monocytes could be patrolling monocytes with CX3CR1 in blood stream.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from cell characteristics.

claim: Resident monocytes with CX3CR1 express CX3CL1 after stimulation with norepinephrine.
source: We previously showed that resident monocytes with CX3CR1 express CX3CL1 after stimulation with norepinephrine, which is produced around the ventral vessels of the spinal cord following activation of the pain-specific neural pathway (Arima et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: There is a CX3CR1-CX3CL1 autocrine loop in the resident monocytes that is regulated by norepinephrine.
source: These results suggested a CX3CR1-CX3CL1 autocrine loop in the resident monocytes that is regulated by norepinephrine.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental observations of chemokine expression and receptor signaling.

claim: CCL5 is required for the recruitment of pathogenic CD4+ T cells, including Th1 and Th17 cells, to the specific vessels from the periphery to trigger micro-inflammation.
source: However, in the current study, there are no CNS-resident activated monocytes in wild type mice under stress. Therefore, CX3CL1, which is a critical chemokine for CNS-resident monocytes, is not critical for the stress-gateway reflex in this study. On the other hand, during the stress-gateway reflex, we recognized CCL5 is required for the recruitment of pathogenic CD4+ T cells, including Th1 and Th17 cells, to the specific vessels from the periphery to trigger micro-inflammation and stimulate the subsequent recruitment of MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of CCL5 blockade.

claim: The recruitment of MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells may be at least partially dependent on CX3CL1 from endothelial cells, which is induced by cytokines from pathogenic CD4+ T cells.
source: We assume that the recruitment of MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells may be at least partially dependent on CX3CL1 from endotheial cells, which is induced by cytokines from pathogenic CD4+ T cells that accumulated at the specific vessels in response to CCL5.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on inference from previous findings and current observations.

claim: MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells had the ability to activate pathogenic CD4+ T cells without exogenous MOG peptide.
source: In agreement, we found that MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells had the ability to activate pathogenic CD4+ T cells without exogenous MOG peptide (Figure 4—figure supplement 5), suggesting that MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells have autoantigen-presentation ability.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: The chemokine/cytokine expression and the accumulation of MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells as well as pathogenic CD4+ T cells at specific vessels could be used to diagnose and/or therapeutically target several types of severe gastrointestinal failure in patients.
source: We theorize that the chemokine/cytokine expression and the accumulation of MHC class IIhiCD11b+ cells as well as pathogenic CD4+ T cells at specific vessels could be used to diagnose and/or therapeutically target several types of severe gastrointestinal failure in patients.
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing potential clinical applications based on the findings.

claim: The development of fatal gastrointestinal failure depended on activation of a previously unidentified DMH-vagal nerve pathway, which was triggered by ATP from the brain micro-inflammation sites.
source: We found that the development of fatal gastrointestinal failure depended on activation of a previously unidentified DMH-vagal nerve pathway, which was triggered by ATP from the brain micro-inflammation sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental data showing the neural pathway and ATP involvement.

claim: This nerve pathway was hardly activated under steady state or stress conditions without brain micro-inflammation.
source: We here found that this nerve pathway was hardly activated under steady state or stress conditions without brain micro-inflammation.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations of neural activation under different conditions.

claim: ATP at the specific vessels can be viewed as a switch that activates this new neural pathway.
source: Thus, ATP at the specific vessels can be viewed as a switch that activates this new neural pathway.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data showing ATP's role in neural activation.

claim: Cerebral microvessels have noradrenergic innervation from the locus coeruleus.
source: For example, it is reported that cerebral microvessels have noradrenergic innervation from the locus coeruleus (Harik, 1986; Kalaria et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on cerebrovascular innervation.

claim: Brain micro-inflammation at some specific vessels could activate unidentified neural pathways to regulate the homeostasis of various organs including brain itself.
source: Our results therefore may indicate that brain micro-inflammation at some specific vessels could activate unidentified neural pathways to regulate the homeostasis of various organs including brain itself.
evidence: This claim is speculative, extrapolating from the current findings to broader implications.

claim: Gastrointestinal diseases after microinjection of cytokines in mice with stress were not suppressed by two antagonists of the corticosteroid receptor such as mifepristone and guggulsterone.
source: Importantly, we found that gastrointestinal diseases after microinjection of cytokines in mice with stress were not suppressed by two antagonists of the corticosteroid receptor such as mifepristone and guggulsterone (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis has a minimum role in the development of micro inflammation-mediated gastrointestinal diseases under stress.
source: Thus, regarding the gastrointestinal response, the resulting vagal nerve activation induced severe gastrointestinal failure, although the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis has a minimum role in the development of micro inflammation-mediated gastrointestinal diseases under stress.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the lack of effect of corticosteroid receptor antagonists.

claim: Pathogenic CD4+ T cells for the transfer EAE express cytokines including IFN-γ, IL-17A, and IL-6.
source: It is known that pathogenic CD4+ T cells for the transfer EAE express cytokines including IFN-γ, IL-17A, and IL-6 (Langrish et al., 2005), and very strong stress alone induces gastric disease via p38 activation at the affected tissues by the activation of the vagal pathway (Debas and Carvajal, 1994; Jia et al., 2007; Uwada et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on T cell cytokine production.

claim: Very strong stress alone induces gastric disease via p38 activation at the affected tissues by the activation of the vagal pathway.
source: It is known that pathogenic CD4+ T cells for the transfer EAE express cytokines including IFN-γ, IL-17A, and IL-6 (Langrish et al., 2005), and very strong stress alone induces gastric disease via p38 activation at the affected tissues by the activation of the vagal pathway (Debas and Carvajal, 1994; Jia et al., 2007; Uwada et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on stress-induced gastric pathology.

claim: Cytokine stimulation in endothelial cells causes the expression of ATP.
source: Moreover, cytokine stimulation in endothelial cells causes the expression of ATP (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cytokines from pathogenic CD4+ T cells act on endothelial cells at the specific vessels and induce ATP around the specific vessels.
source: These results strongly suggested that cytokines from pathogenic CD4+ T cells act on endothelial cells at the specific vessels and induce ATP around the specific vessels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from in vitro and in vivo experimental data.

claim: Several papers have reported concurrence of MS and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD).
source: Several papers have reported concurrence of MS and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) (Gupta et al., 2005; Kimura et al., 2000; Pokorny et al., 2007; Rang et al., 1982; Sadovnick et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature on MS comorbidities.

claim: Primary progressive MS is dominant in patients who suffered from bowel dysfunction.
source: Interestingly, primary progressive MS is dominant in patients who suffered from bowel dysfunction (Preziosi et al., 2013), suggesting that transfer EAE under stress condition could model progressive MS.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to clinical literature.

claim: Transfer EAE under stress condition could model progressive MS.
source: Interestingly, primary progressive MS is dominant in patients who suffered from bowel dysfunction (Preziosi et al., 2013), suggesting that transfer EAE under stress condition could model progressive MS.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on similarities between the model and clinical presentations.

claim: Complications of celiac disease, epilepsy and cerebral calcifications are known to be associated with MS.
source: Complications of celiac disease, epilepsy and cerebral calcifications are also known to be associated with MS (Gobbi, 2005; Gobbi et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature on MS comorbidities.

claim: Micro-inflammations in the brain occur in patients with neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, non-Alzheimer type dementia and Parkinson's disease.
source: It is reported that micro-inflammations in the brain occur in patients with neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, non-Alzheimer type dementia and Parkinson's disease (Appel et al., 2010; Togo et al., 2002), psychological disorder (Najjar et al., 2013), and epilepsy (Vezzani et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on neuroinflammation in various diseases.

claim: Cerebral microbleeding is an important risk factor for dementia.
source: Cerebral microbleeding is an important risk factor for dementia(Watanabe et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to literature on dementia risk factors.

claim: Some neurodegenerative diseases are known to be associated with specific alliles of MHC class II genes.
source: Moreover, some of these diseases are known to be associated with specific alliles of MHC class II genes (Ferrari et al., 2014; Nalls et al., 2014), suggesting involvement of autoreactive CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to genetic association studies.

claim: Micro-inflammation at some vessels could activate new neural pathways to cause dysfunction in the brain neural network and/or in certain organs in the periphery.
source: Based on our findings, we hypothesize that micro-inflammation at some vessels, which is most likely triggerred by autoreactive CD4+ T cells, could activate new neural pathways to cause dysfunction in the brain neural network and/or in certain organs in the periphery.
evidence: This claim is speculative, extrapolating from the current findings to broader disease mechanisms.

claim: The prevalence of dementia is considerably higher in elder people with gastritis.
source: It is reported that the prevalence of dementia is considerably higher in elder people with gastritis and psychological disorders is associated with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) (Momtaz et al., 2014), which supports our hypothesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to epidemiological literature.

claim: Psychological disorders is associated with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
source: It is reported that the prevalence of dementia is considerably higher in elder people with gastritis and psychological disorders is associated with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) (Momtaz et al., 2014), which supports our hypothesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to clinical literature.

claim: Sensitivity to chronic stress in humans is diverse owing to genetic factors and/or environmental factors such as stressful events in early life when the brain is particularly sensitive to stress.
source: Sensitivity to chronic stress in humans is diverse owing to genetic factors and/or environmental factors such as stressful events in early life when the brain is particularly sensitive to stress (Lupien et al., 2009; Mayer, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on stress sensitivity.

claim: Early life stress such as abuse or poor care plays a role in the susceptibility to develop behavior problems and gastrointestinal diseases.
source: Indeed, it is reported that early life stress such as abuse or poor care plays a role in the susceptibility to develop behavior problems and gastrointestinal diseases (Lupien et al., 2009; Mayer, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on early life stress effects.

claim: The early life period is important for the establishment of T cell repertoire and central tolerance.
source: The early life period is also important for the establishment of T cell repertoire and central tolerance, and it is known that thymocytes are very sensitive to glucocorticoid that can be induced by stress (Ashwell et al., 2000; Hogquist et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on T cell development.

claim: Thymocytes are very sensitive to glucocorticoid that can be induced by stress.
source: The early life period is also important for the establishment of T cell repertoire and central tolerance, and it is known that thymocytes are very sensitive to glucocorticoid that can be induced by stress (Ashwell et al., 2000; Hogquist et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to literature on thymocyte biology.

claim: Individual variations to respond to stress might be defined by the presence of autoreactive CD4+ T cells to the CNS autoantigens.
source: Therefore, it is tempting to speculate that individual variations to respond to stress might also be defined by the presence of autoreactive CD4+ T cells to the CNS autoantigens, and that measurement of the autoreactive CD4+ T cell population in the peripheral blood might predict the susceptibility to develop peripheral organ failure by chronic stress.
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing a hypothesis based on the findings.

claim: Measurement of the autoreactive CD4+ T cell population in the peripheral blood might predict the susceptibility to develop peripheral organ failure by chronic stress.
source: Therefore, it is tempting to speculate that individual variations to respond to stress might also be defined by the presence of autoreactive CD4+ T cells to the CNS autoantigens, and that measurement of the autoreactive CD4+ T cell population in the peripheral blood might predict the susceptibility to develop peripheral organ failure by chronic stress.
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing a potential clinical application.

claim: Genetic associations of certain MHC class II alleles with diseases including dementia and neurodegenerative diseases support the hypothesis that autoreactive CD4+ T cells may be involved.
source: Genetic associations of certain MHC class II alleles with diseases including dementia and neurodegenerative diseases etc that involve brain micro-inflammation described above support our hypothesis (Ferrari et al., 2014; Nalls et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from genetic association data cited from literature.

claim: Dysregulations in the peripheral organs including not only gastrointestine and heart but also other organs might affect the status or region of micro-inflammation in the brain.
source: Because there are afferent and efferent neural systems in whole body, it could be possible that dysregulations in the peripheral organs including not only gastrointestine and heart but also other organs might also affect the status or region of micro-inflammation in the brain.
evidence: This claim is speculative, proposing bidirectional interactions between brain and peripheral organs.

claim: Local brain micro-inflammation is induced by stress-mediated PVN activation to enhance the activation of a new neural pathway, the DMH-vagal nerve pathway, to aggravate gastrointestinal failure.
source: We propose that local brain micro-inflammation is induced by stress-mediated PVN activation to enhance the activation of a new neural pathway, the DMH-vagal nerve pathway, to aggravate gastrointestinal failure.
evidence: This claim summarizes the proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.
